description: Run a Go module's (or Go workspace's) container-free tests with statement coverage — `go test -covermode=atomic -coverpkg=./... -coverprofile=build/coverage/cover.out` — and read the profile with a small stdlib Python parser that merges the per-test-binary duplicate blocks `-coverpkg` writes, maps import paths back to repository-relative files, excludes generated files (`// Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.`), and reports the exact statement % for the total and per file (with uncovered line ranges for files under the bar). `-coverpkg=./...` makes code exercised from another package's tests count — including in-process testscript end-to-end tests that run the Cobra command tree, whose re-executed subprocess coverage testscript merges into the profile — so a thin `cmd/<bin>/main.go` and `internal/cli` are measured fairly. Optionally merges a second profile from instrumented binaries (`go build -cover` + `GOCOVERDIR` + `go tool covdata textfmt`). Branch coverage is reported as "not available in Go" (the toolchain measures statements only). Only container-free tests count toward the gate — the `integration` build tag is not set unless asked, and then the result is labeled as not the gate value. Invoke as `/iru-go-coverage [targets]` — `[targets]` is a comma-separated list of Go files (`internal/greet/greet.go`), package directories (`internal/cli`), or import paths — or `/iru-go-coverage` with no argument for whole-module coverage; optional `key: value` lines: `bar: <N>` (default 80), `coverpkg: <pattern>` (default `./...`), `tags: <comma list>`, `run: <regex>` (narrow the tests), `profile: <extra coverprofile>` (merge, e.g. a `covdata textfmt` output), `lock: held`. Reports "coverage not measurable" instead of a false 0% when a target has no statements or lies outside `-coverpkg`. Report-only: never adds tests or modifies source. Use whenever the user (or `iru-go-code-one-task-group` via `iru-gate-runner`) wants to check, or verify a bar for, a Go file, package, or the whole module, instead of reading `go tool cover -func` output by hand.
